facts.text: Huetter is the smallest incorporated city in the United States, covering just 0.04 square miles.
Huetter sits on the Rathdrum Prairie, a broad, flat glacial outwash plain formed by catastrophic Pleistocene floods from Glacial Lake Missoula.
Huetter’s boundaries are defined by local roads, beginning at Huetter Avenue and Boekel Road and looping clockwise to enclose its compact footprint.
Huetter experiences a humid continental climate, with cold snowy winters and warm dry summers shaped by its inland position near the Rocky Mountains.
Huetter is located in Kootenai County, northern Idaho’s panhandle region.
Huetter has struggled with a governance void, as no elected officials have been chosen, prompting neighboring cities to consider annexation.
